[4] Therefore , the metabolic impact of sugar-free Red Bull ( sfRB ) to a comparable amount of caffeine was compared .

[5] REE and respiratory quotient ( RQ ) were measured in eight healthy young men by ventilated-hood indirect calorimetry for @ min baseline and @ h following ingestion of @ ml of either : sfRB + placebo , water +@ mg caffeine , or water + placebo , according to a randomized cross-over design .
[6] sfRB and water + caffeine both increased REE to the same degree ( +@ % ) .
[7] Additionally , sfRB briefly increased RQ .
[8] Water + caffeine had no effect on RQ relative to water + placebo .
[9] sfRB enhanced thermogenesis and marginally shifted RQ to favor carbohydrate oxidation .
[10] The stimulatory effects of sfRB on REE are mimicked by water + caffeine , indicating that the auxiliary ingredients do not influence this thermic effect .
[11] The metabolic effects of sfRB are primarily due to caffeine alone .
